<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user is asking whether volleyball has crowd etiquette similar to tennis.

Volleyball crowds are generally much noisier than tennis. Cheering is expected throughout matches, unlike the quiet, point-by-point style of tennis. Some venues may request silence during serves, but this is not universal.

Indoor and beach volleyball are both louder than tennis. In the Philippines, collegiate and professional indoor games are especially noisy, with chants during serves being common and even encouraged. Official rules generally allow spectator noise without requiring quiet during serves. While some youth or school guides caution against distracting servers, opposing crowds in professional indoor volleyball often try to disrupt them.

No. Volleyball is closer to basketball or Gilas. Noise during serves is normal and even strategic. Tennis is the exception with its quiet-serve rule. This reinforces the blog post's point that volleyball fans learning tennis need the same timing lesson.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

No. Volleyball closer to Gilas than tennis.

**Tennis:** quiet from serve ritual until point dies. Official. Umpire can pause for crowd noise.

**Volleyball:** noise through serve, dig, kill is normal. Opposing gyms often *try* to rattle the server. No universal "shut up on the toss" rule like tennis. PH UAAP/PVL nights built on that din.

So volleyball fans walking into Alex’s match bring same habit problem as Gilas fans — roar on a live serve feels like support there, gets shushed here. Post’s contrast holds.
